title: Finite self-injective dimension of a regular local ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative regular local ring [def-weil-regular-scheme]. In the derived category $D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the complex $A[0]$ is isomorphic to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Thus there exist integers $a\leq b$ and a complex $I^\bullet$ with injective terms, $I^j=0$ for $j\notin[a,b]$, and $A[0]\cong I^\bullet$ in $D(A)$.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, first assertion; with Tag 0A7B, definition-dualizing, and more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-finite-gl-dim] to the given regular local ring $A$. It supplies a finite nonnegative bound $d=\dim A$ such that every $A$-module has a projective resolution of length at most $d$. We shall construct the required injective complex supported in $[0,d]$.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, first two sentences of the proof; algebra.tex Tag 00O7, proposition-regular-finite-gl-dim, final assertion

proof.text: For each $A$-module $M$, apply [lem-weil-pbc-projective-dimension-ext-characterization] with $X=M$ and $n=d$, using the resolution bound from step 1. It gives $\operatorname{Ext}^{i}_A(M,A)=0$ for every $i\ge d+1$, with Ext as in [def-pc-ext]. In particular this vanishing holds for $M=A/T$ for every ideal $T\subseteq A$. No finite-generation restriction on $M$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0AWX, lemma-regular-gorenstein, proof, Ext vanishing; algebra.tex Tag 065R, lemma-projective-dimension-ext, (1) implies (2)

proof.text: The category of $A$-modules is abelian and has enough injectives by [lem-weil-pbc-ring-modules-enough-injectives]. Part (1) of [lem-weil-pbc-left-exact-injective-resolution-degree-zero] therefore gives an exact augmented injective resolution $0\to A\xrightarrow{\varepsilon}I^0\xrightarrow{\partial^0}I^1\to\cdots$, with $I^j=0$ for $j<0$. Put $J=\ker(\partial^d:I^d\to I^{d+1})$ and let $\iota:J\hookrightarrow I^d$ denote its inclusion. For $d=0$, exactness identifies $\varepsilon:A\xrightarrow{\sim}J$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, proof of (3) implies (1), choice of resolution and final kernel; derived.tex Tag 013K, lemma-injective-resolutions-exist, (1)

proof.text: Fix an ideal $T\subseteq A$ and an $A$-linear map $u:T\to J$. Since $I^d$ is injective in the sense of [def-sp-injective-resolutions], extend $\iota u$ to $f:A\to I^d$. The map $\partial^d f$ vanishes on $T$, so it factors as $h\pi$, where $\pi:A\to A/T$ is the quotient map and $h:A/T\to I^{d+1}$. Since $\partial^{d+1}\partial^d=0$ and $\pi$ is surjective, $\partial^{d+1}h=0$. By [lem-weil-pbc-ext-via-injective-resolution] and step 2, $H^{d+1}(\operatorname{Hom}_A(A/T,I^\bullet))=0$. Its explicit cocycle/boundary description gives $g:A/T\to I^d$ with $h=\partial^d g$. Consequently $\partial^d(f-g\pi)=0$, and $f-g\pi$ factors through $J$, giving $v:A\to J$. On $T$ the correction $g\pi$ is zero, so $\iota(v|_T)=\iota u$, and injectivity of $\iota$ gives $v|_T=u$.

source.place: Tag 0A5T, lemma-injective-amplitude, final-kernel argument, with the extension calculation written explicitly; derived.tex Tag 06XR, lemma-compute-ext-resolutions, (1)

proof.text: Step 4 gives the ideal-extension condition for $J$. Apply [lem-sf-baer-criterion] to the commutative ring $A$ and the $A$-module $J$: its hypotheses hold by step 3, and its implication from ideal extensions to injectivity proves that $J$ is injective.

source.place: Tag 0AVF, lemma-characterize-injective-bis, (3) implies (1), as used at the end of Tag 0A5T

proof.text: Define $L^j=I^j$ for $0\le j<d$, $L^d=J$, and $L^j=0$ otherwise. Keep the differentials of $I$ below degree $d-1$ and corestrict $\partial^{d-1}$ to $J$ at the last differential; this is possible because $\partial^d\partial^{d-1}=0$. For $d=0$, simply take $L=J[0]$. The augmentation $A[0]\to L$ is $\varepsilon$ when $d>0$ and its factorization through $J$ when $d=0$. For $d>0$, exactness of the original augmented resolution gives $H^0(L)=A$, zero cohomology for $0<j<d$, and $H^d(L)=J/\operatorname{im}\partial^{d-1}=0$; for $d=0$, the augmentation $A\to J$ is an isomorphism by step 3. All other degrees are zero. Thus this augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism. Every term of $L$ is injective: the $I^j$ by construction, $J$ by step 5, and $0$ because every map into it extends uniquely [def-sp-injective-resolutions]. Quasi-isomorphisms become isomorphisms in [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], so $A[0]\cong L^\bullet$ in $D(A)$; take $a=0$ and $b=d$.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q84-12a55b3dc (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: Read the item, all ten cited node statements, the report, and Stacks 0AWX (dualizing.tex l.3763), 0A5S/0A5T (more-algebra.tex l.17510/17530), 065R, 00O7 and 06XR. The delivery has one commit with two files. It creates no new nodes and leaves the statement, stmt_deps and blueprint unchanged. The statement is 0AWX's finite-injective-dimension conclusion in the 0A5S form; it is not weakened. Step 1 takes gl.dim ≤ d from regular-local-finite-gl-dim. Step 2 takes Ext^{≥d+1}(M,A)=0 for arbitrary M from the 065R node, the all-modules form, as A/T needs. Step 3 builds an exact injective resolution with I^{<0}=0 (enough-injectives + clause (1) of 013K) and sets J=ker ∂^d. Step 4 is a direct Baer test, which I checked line by line: the extension f, ∂^d f=hπ, h a (d+1)-cocycle, then the 06XR node with H^{d+1}=0 gives h=∂^d g, and v=f−gπ restricts to u on T. Edge cases T=0 and T=A hold. This correctly replaces 0A5T's distinguished-triangle argument. Step 5 applies the stated direction of the Baer node (0AVF). Step 6's truncation is a quasi-isomorphism: H^d=J/im ∂^{d-1}=0, with the d=0 and d=1 cases checked, and it is an iso in D(A) by the localization definition. Duplicate search over dag/nodes (0AWX, 0A5T, injective dimension, Gorenstein) found no node stating the item. The generic pbc/sf homological tools outside sk-i-curve-zero are declared in split_report.tool_uses, and I accept them. There is no cycle, no SGA, and the citer is unaffected.
